title: The Biggest and Fastest Things in Space
description:
A volcano 3 times taller than Mount Everest. A star that spins 716 times a second. A cloud colder than empty space. And a star so big our Sun looks like a dot! The Cosmozibs crew hunts the biggest, fastest and coldest records in space.

{{chapters}}

A new episode every day. Join the crew: https://www.youtube.com/@Cosmozibs?sub_confirmation=1

Voices in this video are AI-generated. Every fact is checked with the sources below.

#space #spacefacts #spacerecords

lines.say: Hey, space cadets! Today we're hunting space records. The biggest, the fastest, and the coldest!
A volcano bigger than any mountain on Earth. A star that spins like crazy.
The coldest place we know of. And a star so big, our Sun looks like a crumb next to it!
Records? I hold the record for the longest nap in the asteroid belt.
Four records, four surprises, and a quiz after each one.
I'm going to set a record for the most right answers!
Let's see about that! Ready, set... tick tock, let's go!

short.title: The Biggest Volcano Isn't on Earth

lines.say: The tallest mountain on Earth is Mount Everest. Almost nine kilometers high!
But on Mars, there's a volcano called Olympus Mons. It's about twenty five kilometers tall!
Wait... WHAT? Three times taller than Everest?! How could this happen?!
Yep! You could stack about three Mount Everests and still not reach the top.
And it's super wide too. About six hundred kilometers across. That's about the size of the state of Arizona!
So wide that if you hiked it, the slope would feel almost flat. You'd walk and walk... and walk!
Finally, a mountain worth climbing. Wake me up when we get to the top.
Bonus fact! On Earth, the ground slowly slides around. On Mars, it stays put. So lava kept piling up in the same spot for a very long time!
Like a giant ice cream cone that never stops getting scoops!
And Mars has weaker gravity than Earth. That helps such a huge mountain stand without sinking.
It's the biggest volcano we know of in the whole solar system. And it's quiet now, so no lava party today.
Aww. I brought marshmallows and everything.
Quiz time! About how many Mount Everests tall is Olympus Mons? One, three, or ten?

show.q: How many Everests tall is Olympus Mons?

lines.say: About three! Twenty five kilometers of Martian mountain.
Next record: something that spins faster than anything you've ever seen!

short.title: This Star Spins 716 Times a Second

lines.say: When a giant star explodes, sometimes a tiny leftover is left behind. It's called a neutron star.
Some of them spin incredibly fast. One spins about seven hundred and sixteen times every second!
Wait... WHAT? Seven hundred spins in one second?! How could this happen?!
Think of an ice skater. When she pulls her arms in, she spins faster. A neutron star is a whole star squeezed super small, so it spins super fast!
How small? About twenty kilometers across. That's about the size of a city!
But it's so heavy! One teaspoon of it would weigh about ten million tons. That's like eighty five thousand blue whales!
A teaspoon that heavy? Good luck stirring your hot chocolate.
Bonus fact! Some neutron stars shoot beams of light that sweep around like a lighthouse. We call them pulsars!
When the first pulsar was found in nineteen sixty seven, its beeps were so regular that the team jokingly nicknamed it Little Green Men!
Little green men? Hey! I'm little and green! Was it me?
Sorry, Zib. It turned out to be a spinning star, not aliens. But what a cool mix-up!
Mystery solved. Zib is not a star. Nobody tell him.
Quiz time! About how many times per second can the fastest neutron stars spin? Seven, seventy, or seven hundred and sixteen?

show.q: How fast can a neutron star spin?

lines.say: Seven hundred and sixteen times every second! Faster than a kitchen blender.
Next record: brrr... the coldest place we know of!

short.title: The Coldest Place in the Universe

lines.say: Space is cold. But where is the coldest place we've ever found? It's not Antarctica, and it's not Pluto.
It's a cloud of gas called the Boomerang Nebula. It's about minus two hundred seventy two degrees Celsius!
Wait... WHAT? Colder than a freezer times a thousand?! How could this happen?!
It's only one degree warmer than absolute zero. And nothing can ever get colder than absolute zero!
Here's the weird part. It's even colder than the empty space around it. Empty space is about minus two hundred seventy degrees.
Why? A dying star in the middle blows out gas super fast. And when gas spreads out quickly, it cools down.
Like when you spray a spray can and it gets cold in your hand. Even rocks know that one.
Bonus fact! It's about five thousand light years away, so you don't need a jacket right now.
And scientists on Earth, and on the space station, have made tiny things in their labs that are even colder!
So the coldest place in the universe might be... a science lab?!
For man-made cold, yes! For natural places we know of, the Boomerang Nebula is the champion.
I'm still not visiting. My toes are cold just hearing about it.
Quiz time! Which is the coldest place we know of in nature? Antarctica, Pluto, or the Boomerang Nebula?
The Boomerang Nebula! About minus two hundred seventy two degrees.
And now, the biggest star of today's show. Literally!

short.title: This Star Makes Our Sun Look Tiny

lines.say: Our Sun is huge. About one hundred and nine Earths would fit across it!
But meet VY Canis Majoris. A red hypergiant star. One of the biggest stars ever found!
Wait... WHAT? A star even bigger than the Sun?! How could this happen?!
If you put it where our Sun is, it would stretch past Jupiter, almost all the way out to Saturn!
Earth, Mars and Jupiter would all be inside the star. Our Sun would look like a tiny dot next to it.
And it shines about three hundred thousand times brighter than our Sun!
Three hundred thousand times brighter? Somebody hand that star some sunglasses.
Bonus fact! It's so puffy that it keeps throwing off giant clouds of dust. Now it's hard to see without a telescope!
A star that's so big it hides behind its own dust? That's like hiding behind your own blanket!
Big stars like this don't live very long. Scientists think one day it could end in a huge explosion called a supernova.
Don't worry, it's very far away. And who knows, its leftover could become a speedy neutron star, like the one we just met!
From the biggest to the tiniest! Space is so weird!
Quiz time! If this star replaced our Sun, where would it reach? Mercury, the Moon, or past Jupiter?
Past Jupiter! Almost to Saturn. That's one giant star.
Okay, record hunters, time to speed things up!
Speed round! Five quick facts. Ready? Go!
One! Olympus Mons is about six hundred kilometers wide, about the size of Arizona.
Two! A neutron star is about twenty kilometers across. Smaller than many cities!
Three! Absolute zero is the coldest anything can ever be. About minus two hundred seventy three degrees.
Four! About one hundred and nine Earths fit across our Sun.
Five! Light from the Sun takes about eight minutes to reach us.
Whoa. That's a record number of facts!
Those are four space records! Which one blew your mind the most?
Think about it! The giant volcano, the spinning star, the coldest cloud, or the monster star?
The volcano. Big, rocky, and quiet. Just like me.
Here's a challenge. Ask someone at home what the biggest volcano is. Bet they say Earth!
Tomorrow: how astronauts really live in space!
Subscribe and join the crew. See you tomorrow, space cadets!
